answer: The chairmaker yard rings with the lathe, and chair legs dry in stacks by the wall. Proof of chairmaker via rung turn tally — a rung the chairmaker turns only after 32 rungs sit firm in the leg, each rung turned by the chairmaker himself. quill turns each rung to the gauge, the shavings curling to the floor. sonnet bores the leg true and wedges the rung home. relic sits on the finished chair and rocks it, listening for a creak. Forging this tally takes 32 rungs that never work loose, and the next one still wobbles where the bore ran wide.
